newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Q1 federal revenues up from year earlier.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Q1 federal revenues up from year earlier.

text.p: Swiss federal revenues in the first three months of 1997 rose seven percent from the first quarter a year ago, the Finance Ministry said on Monday.
A ministry statement said the first quarter figures were not enough of a basis to say whether revenues would match projections for the full year.
Revenues from January through March were 5.59 billion Swiss francs, as against 5.32 billion in the year-ago period.
This compared with projected revenues for full 1997 of 34.60 billion and actual 1996 income of 34.16 billion Swiss francs.
"It is too early to tell whether this quarterly amount is on track for the full year or not," a finance ministry spokeswoman told Reuter.
The quarter's total could not simply be multiplied by four for a full-year figure because some taxes and fees flowed in more strongly later in the year, a ministry statement said.
Changes in some tax and fee rules also meant comparisons with earlier quarters were of limited value, it said.
Switzerland is struggling to bring down federal deficits pushed up by six years of zero economic growth and major budget commitments led by social security and agriculture.
The 1996 federal deficit was 315 million Swiss francs over budget at 4.36 billion francs due to lower than expected tax and customs income.
The 1997 federal budget sets a deficit of 5.77 billion Swiss francs, as against a 3.26 billion shortfall in 1995.

The Swiss federal budget has less of a market impact than those in other industrialised countries because of the relatively large volume of spending by the 26 cantons (states) and half-cantons and hundreds of community authorities.
